# Needs assessment — best in class, and what De-Risking Strategies takes from each

**Version 00.00 · revision 0.093** · Project 34 — CrisisCommand Future State

> **Ask.** research best in class needs assessments to help fiends business (operator 2026-09-23)

> **Law.** Two families are needed and they are not the same instrument: the CUSTOMER needs assessment prices the product (S3, S8–S10, S13, S14); the CRISIS needs assessment is the product's own intake (DRS-02, DRS-03, S4, S15, S16). Every method below is SOURCED by URL; what DRS takes from it is DECLARED.

## Customer / product needs assessment

### Outcome-Driven Innovation (Ulwick / Strategyn)

**What it is (SOURCED).** Jobs-to-be-done put into practice: 50–150 desired-outcome statements per job, each {direction, measure, object, context}; the opportunity algorithm ranks importance vs satisfaction; segments are formed by outcome profile, not by industry

**Sources.**

- <https://anthonyulwick.com/outcome-driven-innovation/>
- <https://strategyn.com/jobs-to-be-done/>
- <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outcome-Driven_Innovation>

**What DRS takes (DECLARED).** Every S13 value-driver row and every S14 interview question is written as a desired-outcome statement; the S3 segmentation is validated by outcome profile (the X/Y/Z weights are the first three outcome clusters)

### Voice of the Customer loop (the gate-review template's own method)

**What it is (SOURCED).** Continuous and iterative customer feedback through the stage gates: understand needs vs the next-best alternative → validate concepts with prototypes → evaluate and adapt

**Sources.**

- `docs/drs/sources/01.1_DRS_ProjectResilience_Market_Landscape_Needs_2023.12.06.pdf (p.2–3)`
- `docs/drs/sources/01.1_DRS_Project-AdFusion_Market_Landscape_Needs.pdf (p.2–3)`

**What DRS takes (DECLARED).** The G1→G2 program: three segments × interviews vs the paired NBA before any prototype; the S11/S15/S17 VOC tables of the Pod carry the results

### Kano classification

**What it is (SOURCED).** Must-be · performance · delighter attributes from paired functional/dysfunctional questions; a must-be is not a differentiator

**Sources.**

- <https://asq.org/quality-resources/kano-model>
- <https://citoolkit.com/articles/kano-analysis/>

**What DRS takes (DECLARED).** The 'not differentiators' list (alerting, dashboards, incident logs, messaging, simulations, AAR) are must-be for the NBAs; each S13 row is tagged must-be / performance / delighter in the S16 interviews before it is priced

## Crisis / community needs assessment (the product's intake)

### CDC CASPER — Community Assessment for Public Health Emergency Response

**What it is (SOURCED).** Rapid needs assessment at the household level: two-stage cluster sampling (30 clusters × 7 households), volunteer interview teams, a standard questionnaire, results in days; toolkit 3rd edition 2019

**Sources.**

- <https://www.cdc.gov/casper/media/pdfs/CASPER-toolkit-3_508.pdf>
- <https://cdc.gov/casper/php/overview/index.html>
- <https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4630127/>

**What DRS takes (DECLARED).** DRS-02 needs intake carries CASPER's record shape (who · where · what is lacking · severity · who is responsible · time) so a phone poll is a valid sample of a community, not a shout; the 30×7 design is the fallback when the roster cannot reach everyone

### UN OCHA MIRA — Multi-Sector Initial Rapid Assessment

**What it is (SOURCED).** One common picture across all sectors: situational analysis within 72 hours, MIRA report within two weeks, agreed immediate strategies

**Sources.**

- <https://reliefweb.int/report/world/multi-sector-initial-rapid-assessment-guidance-revision-july-2015-enru>
- <https://emergency.unhcr.org/coordination-and-communication/cluster-system/multi-cluster-sector-initial-rapid-needs-assessment-mira>

**What DRS takes (DECLARED).** The S4 CONOPS clock: authoritative facts and a first needs picture within 72 h; one picture shared by command, responders and the affected population (S6 layers)

### FEMA THIRA / SPR — Threat and Hazard Identification and Risk Assessment / Stakeholder Preparedness Review

**What it is (SOURCED).** Capability targets and the resource requirements to meet them, self-assessed yearly against last year's capability (built, sustained, lost)

**Sources.**

- <https://www.fema.gov/emergency-managers/national-preparedness/goal/risk-capability-assessment>
- <https://www.fema.gov/sites/default/files/2020-07/threat-hazard-identification-risk-assessment-stakeholder-preparedness-review-guide.pdf>
- <https://www.rand.org/pubs/research_reports/RRA2437-1.html>

**What DRS takes (DECLARED).** S15's Conservative / Baseline / Aggressive plans are expressed as capability targets with resource requirements; the trigger for changing plans is a target missed

### FEMA HSEEP — Homeland Security Exercise and Evaluation Program

**What it is (SOURCED).** Exercise design, evaluation and corrective actions that feed the next cycle, informed by risk and capability assessments

**Sources.**

- <https://www.fema.gov/emergency-managers/national-preparedness/exercises/hseep>

**What DRS takes (DECLARED).** S16's Replay → Improve columns are HSEEP corrective actions; the R-CORE loop is HSEEP's cycle with the record kept by the system instead of a binder

### FEMA Community Lifelines

**What it is (SOURCED).** Eight lifelines (Safety and Security · Food, Hydration, Shelter · Health and Medical · Energy · Communications · Transportation · Hazardous Materials · Water) with a status ladder Unstable → Stabilizing → Recovery

**Sources.**

- <https://www.fema.gov/emergency-managers/practitioners/lifelines>
- <https://www.dhs.gov/sites/default/files/2025-01/25_0127_community_lifeline_status_system_fact_sheet.pdf>

**What DRS takes (DECLARED).** The 'what people currently need' list on S2 and the needs-intake categories are the eight lifelines; a lifeline status is the first line of every plan version

### NIMS resource typing + ICS 215 Operational Planning Worksheet

**What it is (SOURCED).** Resources categorized by capability; the ICS 215 lists assignments, resources required vs available and the gap for the next operational period

**Sources.**

- <https://www.fema.gov/emergency-managers/nims/components>
- <https://training.fema.gov/emiweb/is/icsresource/assets/ics%20forms/ics%20form%20215,%20operational%20planning%20worksheet%20(v3).pdf>

**What DRS takes (DECLARED).** DRS-03 resource inventory + gap analysis is an ICS 215 the responders fill from phones; DRS-04 assignments use NIMS typing so a request names a capability, not a brand

### ISO 22301 Business Impact Analysis

**What it is (SOURCED).** Critical activities, maximum acceptable downtime, resources required, financial and non-financial impact of disruption

**Sources.**

- <https://advisera.com/27001academy/knowledgebase/how-to-implement-business-impact-analysis-bia-according-to-iso-22301/>
- <https://www.qmii.com/how-to-conduct-a-business-impact-analysis-bia-in-iso-22301/>

**What DRS takes (DECLARED).** SEG-1's outcome units (outage-hour, production-hour) come from the buyer's own BIA; the S14 interview asks for the BIA's downtime and impact figures before naming any price

## The intake record (CASPER-shaped, lifeline-categorized)

1. who (verified role)
2. where (lifeline + location)
3. what is lacking (lifeline category)
4. severity
5. who is responsible
6. time recorded / time assigned / time fulfilled

## Clocks

| clock | value |
|---|---|
| commonPicture | 72 h (MIRA) |
| report | 2 weeks (MIRA) |
| operationalPeriod | per ICS 215 |

## The outcome-statement format for every value driver and interview question

{direction} {measure} {object} {context} — e.g. 'minimize the time from a recorded need to an assigned responder during a grid outage' (ODI)
